summary.en: Violent clashes continue across South Sudan, with rival groups fighting in Lakes state and an ambush killing five people on a Warrap road, while a drone strike near a displacement camp in Sudan’s Blue Nile killed at least 30, mostly women and children. In Abyei, a market was hit by a drone strike that killed 73 people, and another drone attack in the disputed region killed 153, according to officials. The UCDP recorded 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP. UN Secretary-General Guterres condemned the escalation of drone attacks, and the deputy minister of ICT warned against abusing freedom of expression.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
